issue_context.title: add GetRequiredSection on Configuration (raise exception if missing section)
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @eerhardt, @maryamariyan
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.

It's a little change, and I already finished this implementation. 
I created the pull request
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/40976/files#diff-4efb8afc983c3a36c453768b3802673a

Tagging subscribers to this area: @maryamariyan
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.

Seems useful enough - the current `IConfigurationSection GetSection(string key);` method is documented as:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e8c0a4cb15dad4606c74bc39df3bae33c2ae936e/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Abstractions/src/IConfiguration.cs#L26-L29

Hi @eerhardt
Thanks for your answer but I find it's not enough because it's never return null. And if the section is missing in your config file nothing happen the code continue.
My Goal is if we forget a mandatory section in the configuration file the new '' GetRequiredSection" raise an exception. The method GetSection Return an empty object (and not a null).
Do you understand my goal?
How does this distinguish from a present but empty section?

@ericstj 
I think it's not possible, It's the same of Exists method.
But my goal is if the section is empty or present to have an exception.
If the section is missing or empty it's return false. I reuse the same mechanism
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Abstractions/src/ConfigurationExtensions.cs#L76-L82

@terrajobst 
I think your solution it's also correct. But how to determine if it's better to create an extension method or a new method in the base class. My opinion in this case it's better to put this method on the same place of the GetSection <> GetSectionRequired (both on the same class)

> I think it's not possible, It's the same of Exists method.

It looks like @terrajobst fixed the suggestion to use this.  That addresses my concern.

@terrajobst would an interface addition with a default implementation be better?  ~~Hypothetically an implementer could create a more efficient implementation that doesn't do a double lookup (exists + return).~~  I know we haven't explored default interfaces much in the BCL yet. 

update: actually, i don't think its worth it.  I think the design of IConfigurationSection mitigates the efficiency argument.  I don't see a benefit to forcing / allowing implementers to define their own behavior of this method.  Extension method looks better to me.

@michelcedric, please change your PR to match the API @terrajobst lists here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/40978#issuecomment-675639726, then we can review and merge.

One thing to consider, this *just* missed the cut-off (yesterday) for 5.0 is there any pressing need for you to get this API into the 5.0 release or can it wait for 6.0?

@ericstj 
It's not blocking for me to wait 6.0 but i prefer to use this one as soon as possible in my project. It's a little change finally ;)
